title: Tak Family Trip 3 Days — Dam, Waterfall, Riverside Town | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night family itinerary for Tak, Thailand with kids: Bhumibol Dam, swimmable Lan Sang Waterfall, and the riverside old town on the Ping. Real drive times, entry fees, and spots kids actually enjoy.
keywords: Tak family trip, Tak with kids, Bhumibol Dam, Lan Sang Waterfall, Tak itinerary
h1:
Tak With the Family
3 Days: Dam, Waterfall, Town
intro: Tak is an easier place to bring kids than you'd expect. The distances between the main sights are short, the roads are good, and you get a waterfall you can actually swim in, a big dam with room to walk and take in the view, and a riverside town on the Ping where you can stroll in the evening without rushing. This is a 3-day, 2-night plan paced so the kids don't get worn out and the grown-ups get a real break.

blocks.html: The thing you dread most about a road trip with kids is long hours in the car, long walks, and then a meltdown. Tak handles this well because the main sights all sit within about an hour's drive of town. Several waterfalls are just a few hundred metres' walk from the car park, and Bhumibol Dam has wide open ground for kids to run around. We built this plan around the kids, alternating busier days with easier ones so the balance works.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Tak is good year-round, but if you want the waterfalls running full so the kids can really swim, late rainy season into early cool season (October–December) is best. In the dry months (March–April) some waterfalls run low, so check the national park's page before you go.

items: Day 1 — Tak town, the suspension bridge over the Ping River, the park, and the evening market. An easy day to let the kids settle in.
Day 2 — Bhumibol Dam: walk the dam crest, head up to the viewpoint, and if you have time left, take a raft tour on the reservoir.
Day 3 — Lan Sang Waterfall: a paddle in the shallows and a short nature trail before the drive home.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Tak town on the Ping — an easy day to settle in

items.activity: Arrive in Tak town, check in, have lunch
items.note: Places to stay in town are easy to find, from chain hotels to small resorts. Picking somewhere near the Ping River makes the evening stroll easier.

items.activity: Rest at the room, wait for the sun to soften
items.note: Afternoons in Tak are hot. Let the kids nap or splash around at the hotel first, then head out in the evening.

items.activity: Walk the Rattanakosin Bicentennial Bridge (the suspension bridge)
items.note: This pedestrian suspension bridge runs about 700 metres across the Ping River. It's good for the view, lit up after dark, and kids love the gentle sway underfoot.

items.activity: Let the kids loose at the riverside Chaloem Phrakiat Park
items.note: A riverside park on the Ping with open ground for kids to run and outdoor exercise gear. Locals come for an evening walk and the mood is relaxed.
Tak town has noodle shops, rice porridge, and street snacks. Try khao kriap wow, a local rice-cracker speciality, to take back to the room.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Tak trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Tak
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Bhumibol Dam — Thailand's tallest concrete arch dam

blocks.html: Bhumibol Dam (formerly Yanhi Dam) sits in Sam Ngao district. From Tak town you follow Highway 1 to around km 463–464, then turn off for another 17 kilometres or so, about an hour's drive in total. The dam itself is a concrete arch standing 154 metres from base to crest, the tallest dam of its kind in Thailand. You can walk the crest for views over the reservoir, and there's a viewpoint up top you can drive to. Around it are rest areas and restaurants, a good spot to sit with the kids.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Bhumibol Dam — walk the crest, raft the reservoir

items.activity: Breakfast, then leave Tak town for Bhumibol Dam
items.note: Setting off a little early helps you dodge the midday heat. It's about an hour's drive, with good road the whole way.

items.activity: Walk the dam crest and head up to the viewpoint
items.note: Walk the crest for wide views over the reservoir; the photos are great. Keep a firm hold of the kids' hands, though, since there's a guardrail but a big drop.

items.activity: Wander the rest area around the dam, grab a snack
items.note: There's open ground for kids to run, plus restaurants and cafes. Sit a while and catch the cool breeze off the reservoir.

items.activity: Lunch, then decide whether to carry on or head back
items.note: If you want a full day, follow up with a raft tour in the afternoon. If the little ones are tired, head back to town to rest instead. No need to push it.

items.activity: Raft or boat tour on the reservoir above the dam
items.note: There are raft and boat tours on the reservoir, passing rocky mountains and mid-lake islands like Valentine Island, which you can only reach by boat. Better for families with older kids. Book ahead and check the per-raft price.

blocks.title: Rafting with little ones
blocks.html: If you have kids under 5, think hard about the raft tour, since it runs several hours and keeps you out on the water. Put a life jacket on every child and ask the operator about safety gear before boarding. If it doesn't feel right, just walk the dam instead, you won't miss out.

blocks.text: Lan Sang Waterfall — where kids can actually swim

blocks.html: Lan Sang National Park is in Mae Tho subdistrict, Mueang Tak district, about 20 kilometres from town, an easy half-hour drive. Lan Sang Waterfall steps down in tiers for a total height of around 40 metres. The part kids love is the pool at the bottom, wide and shallow enough to paddle in, and it's a short walk from the car park. The park is open 07:00–17:00, with entry at 20 THB for adults, 10 THB for children, and 40 THB per car. There are restaurants and a cafe inside the park.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Lan Sang Waterfall — a morning swim before the drive home

items.note: Bring a change of clothes, towels, and strap-on sandals with grip. The rocks by the waterfall can be slippery.

items.activity: Arrive at Lan Sang National Park, walk in to the waterfall
items.note: It's a short walk from the car park to the main tier of the falls. The path is easy and kids can manage it on their own.

items.activity: Paddle in the shallow pool, take photos
items.note: Stick to the shallow, still pool and keep a grown-up close the whole time. Don't let kids climb to the upper tiers where the water runs fast.

items.activity: Short nature trail to spot butterflies and trees
items.note: Lan Sang has a short, shady nature trail. Mornings bring out plenty of butterflies, a nice little outdoor classroom for the kids.

items.activity: Lunch near the park or back in town, then drive home
items.note: Hose the kids off and change them before getting in the car so the ride home is comfortable.

blocks.text: More to add if you have the time

blocks.html: If the family has more than 3 days or you want to add a day of nature, there are several more spots in Tak that work with kids. Just gauge it by the children's age and stamina, since some places involve longer hikes.

items.name: Taksin Maharat National Park
items.blurb: Home to a giant krabak tree so huge it takes more than ten people linking arms to circle it, plus a natural stone bridge. You can reach the big tree on a short walk, but parts of the trail are steep and long, so it suits older kids who can handle the distance.

items.name: Rim Moei Market, Mae Sot
items.blurb: A border market on the Moei River, with Myawaddy, Myanmar on the far bank. It sells local goods and unusual snacks, a chance for kids to see a different culture. But it's in Mae Sot district, far from Tak town and over the mountains.

blocks.title: Making Tak easy with kids
blocks.html: Always keep snacks and water in the car, since some stretches between sights have no convenience stores. Put sunscreen and bug spray on the kids before the waterfalls and parks, and plan rest days between active ones so the kids don't burn out.

faq.q: How many days should we spend in Tak with young kids?
faq.a: 3 days and 2 nights is about right, covering Tak town, Bhumibol Dam, and Lan Sang Waterfall without rushing. With very young kids you can trim it to 2 days, picking just Tak town and the nearby Lan Sang Waterfall, and still have a great time.

faq.q: Which waterfall in Tak can kids swim in?
faq.a: Lan Sang Waterfall in Lan Sang National Park is the best pick, since it's only about 20 kilometres from town, a short walk from the car park, and has a shallow pool kids can paddle in. Entry is 20 THB for adults and 10 THB for children.

faq.q: Is Bhumibol Dam suitable for kids?
faq.a: It's good for taking in the view and letting kids run in the open ground. The dam crest is very high, so hold their hands carefully. The reservoir raft tour suits older kids more than little ones, and everyone should wear a life jacket.

faq.q: Are the distances between sights in Tak long?
faq.a: The main sights in this plan are short drives. Lan Sang Waterfall is about 20 kilometres from town and Bhumibol Dam is about an hour's drive, with good road the whole way. It suits families coming in their own car.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Tak with the family?
faq.a: Late rainy season into the cool season, October to December, is best, with comfortable weather and plenty of water in the falls. In the dry months of March to April some waterfalls run low, so check before you go.
